title: nc why <task-id>: one screen of evidence per task
objective: Add a `why` subcommand to nc/cli.py that prints, for one task: its status, acceptance criteria, every run (agent, role, outcome, duration, log path), every message about it, and the stored acceptance check output from $NC_HOME/checks/<task>.txt. This is how the owner reviews accepted work without reading the database by hand.
acceptance: A test builds a task with runs and messages and asserts the output contains the outcome of each run and the check output
An unknown task id exits non-zero with a clear message rather than a traceback
boundaries: Only touch nc/cli.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not change the database schema, the scheduler or the protocol

title: Garbage-collect stale worktrees
objective: Add `nc gc`: for every task that is done or blocked, remove its git worktree under $NC_HOME/work and prune, leaving the branch itself intact. Print what was removed. The Orange Pi has little disk, and a worktree per attempted task accumulates forever today.
acceptance: A test creates a worktree for a done task and one for an in_progress task, runs gc, and asserts only the first is gone and its branch still exists
gc never touches a worktree whose task is queued, in_progress or in_review
boundaries: Only touch nc/cli.py, nc/arbiter.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not change the database schema or the scheduler

title: Escalate agents that have been blocked too long
objective: The scheduler must notice when an agent has been blocked on an unanswered question for longer than Config.ask_timeout_s and raise an incident once per agent (not once per cycle), so a forgotten question surfaces in `nc incidents` instead of silently stalling the queue. Add the check to Scheduler.run before picking an agent.
acceptance: A test with ask_timeout_s=0 asserts exactly one incident is raised for a blocked agent even after several run cycles
An agent blocked for less than ask_timeout_s produces no incident
boundaries: Only touch nc/scheduler.py, nc/state.py and files under tests/
Do not change the turn protocol or the outcome handlers

title: Record what each turn cost
objective: Token counts are parsed from CLI output only by a loose regex today and are usually NULL. Make nc/adapters.py extract the token usage that `codex exec` actually reports (inspect a real log under $NC_HOME/runs), fall back to NULL when absent, and add `nc costs` printing tokens and wall-clock time per task and per role from the run table.
acceptance: A test feeds a real codex log sample to the parser and asserts the token count
costs works on an empty database without crashing
boundaries: Only touch nc/adapters.py, nc/cli.py and files under tests/
Do not change how sessions are launched

title: Per-role adapters and a working Claude path
objective: Config.models maps role to model, but the adapter is global. Allow config to select an adapter per role (for example worker=codex, critic=claude), so the critic can be a different vendor from the worker — an independent reviewer is worth more when it does not share the author's blind spots. Verify the claude adapter's argument list against the installed CLI at /root/.local/bin/claude and fix it if wrong.
acceptance: A test asserts the scheduler asks for the adapter named in config for each role and falls back to the global adapter when unset
The claude command line is documented in the README as verified against the installed CLI version
boundaries: Only touch nc/config.py, nc/adapters.py, nc/scheduler.py, README.md and files under tests/
Do not spend a turn running paid sessions; a --version or --help probe is enough
